"Use the substitution $u=x^{3} + 2$. Which integral is obtained?

$$
\int x^{2} e^{x^{3} + 2}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "f7131eaa-146e-51c1-a2fb-f1a082e72cea" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=x^{3} + 2$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(3 x^{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int x^{2} e^{x^{3} + 2}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

The transformed integral is

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).
$$"] [:db/add "f7131eaa-146e-51c1-a2fb-f1a082e72cea" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "f7131eaa-146e-51c1-a2fb-f1a082e72cea" :question/answer-fields
